description: Tenant invoice should go out within this many days after the agency pays the water bill
basis: Internal target. NSW only allows charging a tenant if the agent asks within 3 months of the bill being issued (nsw.gov.au water rules), so 30 days leaves a safety margin

description: After this many days a water bill may no longer be chargeable to the tenant (flagged as may_be_unrecoverable)
basis: NSW: request payment within 3 months of the bill being issued; the bill-issue date is not in the lists, so the date the agency paid is used

description: Tenant should pay within this many days after the invoice is sent
basis: NSW: the tenant must be given at least 21 days to pay a water usage charge

description: A weekly rent above this is the whole unit; at or below is one room
A step is due soon when its deadline is within this many days
basis: One week of warning is the usual horizon for a small agency

description: A property should not have more routine inspections than this in 12 months
basis: NSW residential tenancy rules allow routine inspections up to 4 times a year

description: Tenant should be told at least this many days before a routine inspection
basis: NSW: 7 days written notice for routine inspections

description: Leases ending within this many days are listed for renewal
basis: NSW needs 60 days notice of a rent increase on renewal, so renewals are planned about two months ahead

description: Reference only: rent must be this many days overdue before a termination notice can be given in NSW
basis: NSW: 14 days overdue, then at least 14 days notice. Not computed yet because it needs weekly rent due dates
